item.title: Araghchi condoles Italy over death of two nationals in Kuwait oncident
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and his Italian counterpart, Antonio Tajani, held a phone conversation on Thursday evening to discuss issues of mutual concern. During the call, Araghchi expressed regret over the deaths of two Italian nationals in a drone incident in Kuwait and extended his condolences and sympathy to the Italian government and people. Rejecting as baseless the accusations against Iran over the incident, Araghchi stressed that Iran had no role or involvement whatsoever in it. He also announced Tehran's readiness to cooperate with the governments of Kuwait and Italy to establish the origin of the incident and investigate its various aspects.

item.title: FM Araghchi rejects claims of Iranian role in Kuwait drone incident
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi held a phone conversation with his Kuwaiti counterpart, Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, on Thursday afternoon. During the call, Araghchi categorically rejected claims that Iran had carried out a drone attack on Kuwait, stressing that the Islamic Republic had no involvement whatsoever in the incident. Expressing regret over the human casualties and damage caused by the incident, Araghchi also announced Iran's readiness to conduct a joint investigation with the Kuwaiti side to thoroughly examine the incident and identify its source and the parties involved.

item.title: Iranian South Korean FMs discuss bilateral ties regional developments
item.description: South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun held a phone conversation with his Iranian counterpart, Seyed Abbas Araghchi, on Thursday morning to discuss bilateral issues and the latest regional developments. During the call, Araghchi warned against any foreign military presence in the region, stressing that the deployment of foreign forces would not help establish stability and security, but would instead escalate tensions and widen the scope of conflicts. He also briefed his South Korean counterpart on the latest diplomatic efforts and initiatives aimed at preserving regional peace and stability, outlining Iran's firm positions and views on the requirements and framework for achieving peace in the region. Cho, for his part, reaffirmed South Korea's commitment to supporting regional peace and stability and assured Araghchi that Seoul had no intention of intervening in or participating in the war and had no plans to deploy troops to the region. He expressed hope that a peaceful solution could be found to end the ongoing war and tensions.

item.title: Iranian Foreign Ministry spox expresses sympathy with families of Egypt fire victims
item.description: Following a fire caused by the overturning and subsequent ignition of a fuel tanker in Egypt’s Giza Governorate, which left more than 50 people dead and injured, Esmail Baqaei, Spokesperson for the Iranian Foreign Ministry, expressed the condolences and sympathy of the government and people of the Islamic Republic of Iran to the bereaved families, as well as to the government and people of Egypt. He also prayed to Almighty God to grant patience and fortitude to the bereaved families and a speedy recovery to those injured.

item.title: Iranian Foreign Minister condemns Israeli regime’s lies about Iran’s Pharmaceutical industry
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi issued a statement condemning the Israeli regime’s fabrications concerning Iran’s pharmaceutical industry. The statement reads: The Israeli regime has refused to join any international convention prohibiting nuclear, chemical, or biological weapons. It possesses hundreds of nuclear warheads, has attacked seven countries in the region, and occupied parts of the territories of three countries. Over the past year alone, Israel has twice dragged the United States into a failed war against Iran. Now, this same warmongering regime shamelessly accuses Iran, a country that is a member of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) and the Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW), and which was itself a victim of chemical weapons supplied by West Germany to Saddam Hussein’s regime, of producing and concealing such heinous weapons in pharmaceutical factories!! The purpose behind making such an outrageous allegation is clear: to deceive the United States into being dragged into another war in pursuit of Israel’s interests, while simultaneously putting Iranian patients at risk.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran strongly condemns the Israeli regime’s airstrikes and artillery attacks on various areas in southern Lebanon and the destruction of civilian infrastructure in the country, and emphasizes Lebanon’s inherent right to defend its territorial integrity and national sovereignty. The escalation of the Israeli regime’s acts of aggression against Lebanon, coinciding with the celebrations marking the country’s independence, constitutes a flagrant violation of the UN Charter and the November 2024 ceasefire agreement. It also lays bare the undeniable truth that the Zionist enemy poses the greatest threat to Lebanon’s independence, territorial integrity, security and stability. Undoubtedly, the Israeli regime’s commission of grave international crimes, including genocide, and its flagrant violations of international law in Gaza and the West Bank, Lebanon, Syria and other countries across the region warrant a firm response from the United Nations and the international community. However, the United States, as Israel’s biggest supporter and accomplice, has prevented any effective action in this regard. The Security Council’s inaction in the face of the occupation of vast areas of Lebanon and the continuation of acts of aggression against the country, carried out with the support and complicity of the United States and certain other Western countries, has not only undermined the credibility of this body but has also emboldened the Israeli regime to further violate the law and commit grave crimes. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs also condemns the United States’ destructive interference in Lebanon’s internal affairs and warns that Washington’s moves to establish mechanisms lacking national consensus in Lebanon, aimed at paving the way for the advancement of the Israeli regime’s sinister and expansionist objectives, not only fail to serve Lebanon’s national rights and interests and cannot prevent the Israeli regime’s occupation, expansionism, aggression and terrorism against Lebanon, but will also pose serious threats to the country’s independence, security, stability and national cohesion. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while paying tribute to the steadfastness and resilience of the noble people of Lebanon in confronting the Israeli regime’s military aggression and expansionism, reaffirms the Islamic Republic of Iran’s support for Lebanon in its efforts to defend its independence, national sovereignty and territorial integrity.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran strongly condemns the crimes of the Zionist regime against the oppressed people of Palestine, particularly in Gaza, and emphasizes the urgent need for effective action by the international community to stop the genocide and to hold the Zionist criminals accountable and punish them. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs also strongly condemns the crimes of the occupying regime and the terrorist acts of Zionist settlers against Palestinians in the West Bank—the most recent of which was the burning of the Al-Dahi Mosque. While Gaza has been turned into a pile of rubble and debris as a result of extensive bombings, and the displaced people of Gaza have been deprived even of access to tents to protect themselves from the cold and rain in the winter cold, Zionist military forces, by storming the center of Gaza, are seeking to intensify the genocide plan and kill more people. The inaction imposed on international institutions by the United States and the supporters of the occupying regime has led to greater insolence by this regime and the continuation of the gross violation of the fundamental rights of the Palestinian people. Without a doubt, the United States and other supporters of the occupying regime—especially Germany as the second-largest arms seller to this regime, as well as the United Kingdom, France, and Canada, which in various ways have shielded this regime from any accountability and punishment—are partners in the crimes committed in Gaza. Furthermore, all parties that were present and participated in the ceasefire agreement of 9 October 2025 in Sharm El-Sheikh bear direct responsibility for stopping the crimes of the occupying regime. The Islamic Republic of Iran recalls the responsibility of all states, in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations and international law, to support the oppressed people of Palestine in realizing their right to self-determination and liberation from the evil of occupation, apartheid, and brutal colonialism, and emphasizes that all countries, pursuant to the relevant international instruments, particularly the “Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide” and the “Four Geneva Conventions of 1949,” are obligated to take action to stop the genocide and war crimes that are continuously taking place in Gaza and the West Bank. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs also condemns the continuous obstruction by the American ruling establishment of the process of addressing the crimes committed by the Zionist regime, especially through the sanctions and intimidation of the judges of the International Criminal Court, and reminds all countries of their responsibility to prosecute and punish the leaders of the Zionist regime for the commission of international crimes. The Islamic Republic of Iran, while emphasizing its all-out support for the Palestinian people until the realization of their right to self-determination and the establishment of an independent Palestinian state with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital, calls on the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and all Islamic countries to take immediate measures to utilize all the capacities of this organization and other international institutions to confront the genocide of the Palestinians.
